import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio

# Set renderer for Colab
pio.renderers.default = 'colab'

# Ensure date format
Walmart_df2['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(Walmart_df2['Date'])

# Sort data
Walmart_df2 = Walmart_df2.sort_values('Date')

# Create chart
fig = px.line(
    Walmart_df2,
    x='Date',
    y='Weekly_Sales',
    title='Trend Analysis of Walmart Weekly Sales',
    markers=True
)

# Tooltip
fig.update_traces(
    hovertemplate=
    '<b>Date:</b> %{x|%d-%b-%Y}<br>' +
    '<b>Weekly Sales:</b> $%{y:,.2f}<extra></extra>'
)

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white',
    xaxis_title='Date',
    yaxis_title='Weekly Sales'
)

fig.show()

In [12]:
# Calculate correlation matrix for numerical features
numerical_cols = ['Weekly_Sales', 'Temperature', 'Fuel_Price', 'CPI', 'Unemployment']
correlation_matrix = Walmart_df[numerical_cols].corr()
print("Correlation Matrix:")
display(correlation_matrix)

# Prepare data for line chart (Weekly_Sales vs. Temperature over Time)
df_for_correlation_plot = Walmart_df[['Date', 'Weekly_Sales', 'Temperature']].copy()
df_for_correlation_plot['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df_for_correlation_plot['Date'], format='%d/%m/%Y')
df_for_correlation_plot = df_for_correlation_plot.sort_values('Date')

# Create the dual-axis line chart
fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))

color = 'tab:red'
ax1.set_xlabel('Date')
ax1.set_ylabel('Weekly_Sales', color=color)
ax1.plot(df_for_correlation_plot['Date'], df_for_correlation_plot['Weekly_Sales'], color=color, label='Weekly Sales')
ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color)

ax2 = ax1.twinx()  # instantiate a second axes that shares the same x-axis
color = 'tab:blue'
ax2.set_ylabel('Temperature', color=color)
ax2.plot(df_for_correlation_plot['Date'], df_for_correlation_plot['Temperature'], color=color, label='Temperature')
ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color)

fig.tight_layout()  # otherwise the right y-label is slightly clipped
plt.title('Weekly Sales vs. Temperature over Time')
plt.show()

print("\nTo visualize correlation with other factors, you can change 'Temperature' to 'Fuel_Price', 'CPI', or 'Unemployment' in the line chart code above.")
print("For a more direct view of correlation coefficients across all numerical factors, consider using a heatmap: plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6)); sns.heatmap(correlation_matrix, annot=True, cmap='coolwarm'); plt.title('Correlation Heatmap'); plt.show()")
